description:
Somos a Without Limits, uma equipa inovadora de Luanda focada no desafio Be An Earth System Trend Detective! Unimos paixão por tecnologia, programação avançada e ciência da Terra para decifrar tendências ambientais globais através de soluções baseadas em dados.

Procuramos colaboradores entusiastas com experiência em Design Gráfico, Estatística ou Gestão de Dados para enriquecer a nossa equipa. Vem construir o futuro connosco!
summary:
Ground Truth Africa is an open-source climate trend detection and data-artifact auditing platform for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Analyzing 25 years (2001–2025) of monthly Earth-system data across 56 locations in 7 African regions and 5 seasonal aggregations, it pairs non-parametric trend statistics (Sen's slope, Trend-Free Pre-Whitening Mann-Kendall, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control) with automated two-source cross-validation against ECMWF ERA5 and NASA/JAXA GPM IMERG. Rather than accepting single-reanalysis trends at face value, the system flags and eliminates spurious trends, step artifacts (such as a 2007–2008 MERRA-2 jump in Bangui), and unconfirmed regional "mirrors." details:
What it does: Ground Truth Africa enables users and researchers to explore, quantify, and audit multi-decadal climate trends (2001–2025) across 56 African locations and 7 regions (anual, DJF, MAM, JJA, SON), as well as run on-demand trend analysis for any custom coordinate in Africa via POST /api/v1/analyze.

How it works:

  1. Multi-Source Ingestion & Caching: Fetches monthly NASA POWER data (13 variables from MERRA-2 and CERES/FLASHFlux), daily ECMWF ERA5 data via Open-Meteo, and monthly GPM IMERG v07 precipitation via USF IMaRS ERDDAP, caching all raw payloads locally and storing 3,640 series in SQLite (ground_truth.db) and trends.json.
  2. Non-Parametric Statistical Engine: Computes annual and meteorological seasonal means (requiring ≥15 valid years), applies conditional Trend-Free Pre-Whitening (TFPW; Yue et al., 2002) when lag-1 autocorrelation |r₁| > 1.96 / √n​, runs a tie-corrected two-sided Mann-Kendall test, estimates Sen's slope per decade, evaluates 4-sub-window sign robustness, and applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (N=56N = 56N=56) per (variable, season).
  3. Cross-Validation & Artifact Filtering: Compares NASA POWER trends against ERA5 (temperature/humidity) and GPM IMERG (precipitation), assigning verdicts (confirmed, partial, not_confirmed, implausible_level_or_corr, unverified, unvalidated). Separates opposing-sign pairs into local mirror (≤ 1 500 km) vs. regional_contrast (> 1 500 km).
  4. Key Findings ("Five Detective Cases"): Confirms a sharp 2022–2025 Mediterranean warming jump (e.g., Algiers: +1.22 °C (MERRA-2) / +1.23 °C (ERA5), r = 0.98) and persistent Angola warming (Luanda, Huambo, Ondjiva), while exposing and discarding unconfirmed MERRA-2 cooling in Khartoum, Juba, and Cape Town, a 2007–2008 MERRA-2 step artifact in Bangui, and an IMERG grid-cell anomaly in Addis Ababa.

Tools & Tech Stack:

  • Backend & Stats: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, SQLite, NumPy, HTTPX, Typer, Rich, Pytest (94 passing tests), Ruff.
  • Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL, D3.js, TanStack Query, Zustand, i18next (English & Portuguese).
